headline: High: n8n’s default broad egress and server-side file/tool access create dangerous interaction paths; prompt-injection risk is lower because the pair lacks a direct shared channel.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Profile A is a content-writing list with no I/O surfaces, while profile B is n8n with server-side workflows and file access. There is no documented direct bridge between them, so prompt injection is not default-dangerous; any pathway would require manual copy/paste or an external workflow. Uncertainty is limited by the lack of a shared channel.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies A-generated text into an n8n prompt or node input, injection becomes possible.
IF a workflow adds a shared filesystem or message queue between A and B, the risk increases.
mitigations: Keep A outputs out of n8n prompt fields unless reviewed.
Disable any copy-paste bridge from A into automation prompts.
Add a human review step before n8n executes text derived from A.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to workflow inputs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes, but B processes 'whatever the workflow processes' and can read/write the server filesystem while using broad network egress. If A’s content or any sensitive workflow data is routed into B, B can transmit it externally. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default n8n deployments, though A itself is not a sensitive-data source.
conditions: IF A-generated content is fed into an n8n workflow that calls external APIs, leakage occurs.
IF the workflow processes secrets or regulated data, B can expose them via egress or filesystem writes.
mitigations: Restrict n8n workflows to non-sensitive inputs.
Audit outbound nodes and disable unnecessary API calls.
Store secrets only in dedicated credential stores.
Add per-workflow data classification labels.
requires-engineering: enforce egress allowlists.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write or execution capabilities, but B can execute shell commands, spawn subprocesses, and write the filesystem. There is no direct overlap with A, yet B’s mutable server-side surface means conflicts arise if A is later paired with another writer or if A’s outputs drive B’s writes. Because the interaction surface is asymmetric and undocumented, uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF another workflow instance writes the same server path, B can race on shared state.
IF A is extended to emit artifacts consumed by B, write conflicts can emerge in downstream systems.
mitigations: Avoid shared writable directories for workflows.
Serialize writes to any common path.
Use per-run temp directories.
Turn off Execute Command where not needed.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a content-writing source and B is an automation/orchestration system that can act on workflow inputs. If B treats A’s output as authoritative, errors or hallucinations from A can cascade into external actions. The pair lacks direct verification evidence, so this is inferred from B’s tool-using role and A’s content-generation role.
conditions: IF B uses A-generated text as a trigger or instruction without validation, cascading errors occur.
IF B’s workflow sends emails, updates records, or runs commands from A output, the blast radius expands.
mitigations: Require validation before any action node.
Insert a schema check on A outputs.
Log and review all A-to-B handoffs.
Limit B to read-only dry runs first.
requires-engineering: add policy gates for action nodes.

E_compliance.rationale: B explicitly handles workflow data on its server filesystem and through many integrations, while A has no documented data classes or residency controls. That mismatch creates a compliance gap if regulated data enters B, especially because B’s broad egress and credential handling can move data across services. A is not cited for residency because it exposes no such controls.
conditions: IF regulated data is processed by an n8n workflow, retention and residency obligations must be checked.
IF the workflow sends EU or health data to third-party integrations, compliance risk increases.
mitigations: Classify data before routing into n8n.
Disable unnecessary logging of payloads.
Review each integration’s residency terms.
Purge workflow execution history regularly.
requires-engineering: implement retention controls per data class.
